newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat to announce taking on workers -paper.
newsitem.headline: Fiat to announce taking on workers -paper.

text.p: Italian car maker Fiat is expected to announce soon that it will hire up to 2,000 workers after an eight-year hiring freeze, an Italian newspaper reported on Tuesday.
La Repubblica daily said the news would be released officially to unions, probably on Wednesday.

It said some 1,000 of those expected to be hired would be taken on in the area of Turin, Fiat's home city in northwestern Italy, and with activity concentrated on the Mirafiori plant which produces small and medium-sized vehicles.
The newspaper said Fiat appeared to want to address a recent rise in orders by employing people on fixed term contracts.
It said Fiat's Mirafiori and Rivalta plants had not taken on workers since 1989, except for people under 29 on training contracts.
A spokesman for Fiat said the company would release a statement later but gave no further details.
Italian car orders have been given a shot in the arm by the start of a government incentive scheme in January which encourages consumers to scrap cars 10 years or more old and buy new ones.
